# Write the animal file

## Job

Write the animal file for one species: its body, behaviour, food, year
and English text, in the shape of the example animals.

## Input

The surveyed species:

```
{
  "species": "herring",
  "latin": "Clupea harengus",
  "habitats": [
    "sea"
  ],
  "length_cm": 45.0,
  "note": "The main animal's prey; write its year and food from the region's foods and cast above."
}
```

Its GBIF taxon, already decided (copy the block exactly):

```
{
  "gbif_key": 8351946,
  "rank": "SPECIES",
  "name": "Clupea harengus"
}
```

Its role in this region: prey.

The region's food kinds (every `diet` kind must be one of these):

```
water_bugs, water_plants
```

The region's cast:

```
blue_tang, butterflyfish, clownfish, lionfish
```

Tags the cast's existing animals carry (every `hunts` entry must be
one of these; `hunts` names prey tags, never animal ids):

```
fish, small_fish
```

Tags the cast's hunters need that no existing cast animal carries
(a new species must carry the ones that fit it):

```

```

Tags the existing animals carry (`tag: files`):

```
amphibian: frog
big_fish: pike, reef_shark
bird: herring_gull, mallard
fish: blue_tang, bream, butterflyfish, clownfish, lionfish, perch, pike, reef_shark, roach, young_perch, young_roach
frog: frog
fry: young_perch, young_roach
insect: bee
large_mammal: bottlenose_dolphin, moose
lizard: lizard
mammal: bottlenose_dolphin, saimaa_seal
predator: fox
reptile: green_sea_turtle, lizard
seal: saimaa_seal
small_bird: chaffinch, great_tit, kestrel, mallard
small_fish: blue_tang, butterflyfish, clownfish, perch, roach
small_mammal: flying_squirrel, mountain_hare, squirrel, vole
vole: vole
```

The archetypes to choose from: amphibian, animal, bird, fish, insect, land_mammal, reptile.

Its model file, already decided (T16 builds it; write the path exactly):

```
res://assets/animals/herring.glb
```

# Describe the model's edits

## Job

Describe how Atlantic herring (Clupea harengus) differs from the roach model,
as a short list of edits. Code scales the reference to the real
size and applies the edits; it moves positions and sizes together,
so parts keep overlapping. Never write positions or sizes: only
colours, factors, marks and repaints.

## Input

What the adult looks like:

Atlantic herring (Clupea harengus), about 45.0 cm long: the main animal's prey. Colours: dark blue-green, silvery white. Marks: single short dorsal fin midway, deeply forked tail, protruding lower jaw.
{
  "length_cm": 45.0
}

The reference table's line for its kind:

What the `roach` model looks like (1.0 keeps this): Roach (Rutilus rutilus)
(the species is not on the reference table)

The reference spec's parts (name, colour, bone role):

- body: side, body
- back: back, body
- belly: belly, body
- head: side, body
- crown: back, body
- snout: side, body
- rear: side, fin
- rear_back: back, fin
- stalk: side, fin
- stalk_end: side, fin
- dorsal: fin, body
- anal: fin_red, fin
- tail_top: fin, fin
- tail_low: fin, fin
- tail_mid: fin, fin
- pelvic_l: fin_red, body
- pectoral_l: fin_red, body
- mouth_l: dark, body
- eye_l: eye, body
- pupil_l: dark, body

## Output

Strict JSON only: the edits object, no fences, no commentary.
The schema arrives with the call; its shape:

- `colors`: every reference colour name to its hex on this
  animal, like "#7a4a2b". Keep a colour when the survey names
  none.
- `new_colors`: more colours the animal needs, as
  `{"name", "hex"}` pairs; usually empty.
- Seven factors, numbers 0.4 to 2.5, 1 meaning as the
  reference: `head` (the head, whole), `muzzle` (the face in
  front of the eyes), `ears`, `leg_thickness` (legs' width,
  never length), `paws` (the lowest part of each leg),
  `body_girth` (the body's width and depth), `tail_width`.
  `muzzle` is a mammal's face; a bird's is its `bill`. A bird
  reference offers three more, only when the schema n…<3909 chars>

new_colors.description: More colours the animal needs; usually empty

unmakable.description: Marks the animal has that no edit above can make (a mane, antlers), as plain words

key_marks.description: The one or two marks that make the species known, from the research's looks, as plain words; empty only when the looks name none

bands.description: Wide body bands, 1 to 5, when the looks name bands or bars; 0 when they name none

band_color.description: The bands' colour name from colors or new_colors; empty when bands is 0

# Check the render's marks

## Job

Look at the render of Atlantic herring and say which of its key
marks show. These marks make the species known; a child
must see them at game distance. Judge only what the
render shows, never what the species should have.

## Input

The key marks:

- dark blue-green back with silvery white belly
- deeply forked tail

The render is attached.

## Output

Strict JSON only: the review object, no fences, no
commentary. The schema arrives with the call; its shape:

- `shown`: the key marks the render shows, in the input's
  words.
- `missing`: the key marks the render lacks, in the input's
  words.

Every key mark lands in exactly one of the two. A mark
that shows faintly or partly still shows.

## Stop

Write the review once.

shown.description: The key marks the render shows

missing.description: The key marks the render lacks
